title: Service Cloud Voice – Channel Setup & IVR Flow

data_model.signal: No new objects; writes to native Voice Call record fields only.

automation.signal: Service Cloud Voice Flow: greeting → role capture → category capture → FID lookup → Omni-Channel route → after-hours branch. ~15–20 nodes, conditional logic, 2 DML paths. Declarative/Flow-only.

integration.signal: Toll-free number provisioning on Amazon Connect OEM or BYOT — Salesforce-managed telephony bridge. No custom API callout needed.

ui.signal: IVR is a Voice Flow — no LWC build.

sharing_security.signal: IVR disclosure script in greeting. Recording retention config. Standard profile/permission access.

size_rationale: M — driven by IVR Flow branching complexity (5+ paths, role+category+FID capture, after-hours branch). All other dimensions XS–S. Assumes toll-free provisioning is Salesforce-native (no bespoke telephony work).
risks: Number provisioning lead time unknown (Open Q4: Amazon Connect OEM vs BYOT). Delay here gates the entire voice channel. BYOT adds ~S of additional integration config.

title: Omni-Channel QSR Skill & Routing Config

data_model.signal: No new objects. Omni-Channel skill, queue, presence are native config.

automation.signal: Queue operating hours rules + after-hours routing branch. Minimal Flow automation.

sharing_security.signal: Omni-Channel presence config, capacity settings, agent assignment to QSR skill. Standard profile-level.

ui.signal: Omni-Channel widget is native Service Console component — no custom LWC.

size_rationale: M — breadth: QSR skill + 3 warm-transfer queues (AJ Claessens, Spark driver, Compliance on-call) + presence/capacity + operating hours config + callback queue. Each piece is S but the set of 5–6 distinct configuration objects compounds to M.
risks: Coverage hours decision open (Open Q1). Spanish bilingual coverage TBD — could add +S if a separate skill/overflow queue is needed. Compliance on-call queue does not exist today: ownership + staffing needed before config can complete.

title: Voice Call → Case Linkage & Service Console Layout

data_model.signal: LMD disposition picklist + custom fields on Case. RecordType=Complaint. Voice Call object linked to Case (native pinning).

automation.signal: Flow on Voice Call Accepted: SOQL match by phone/FID/30-day window, conditional link vs. auto-create, write role+category to Voice Call record, set Case fields, trigger sub-tab. ~25–30 nodes, 3+ DML paths, recursion considerations. Validation rule blocks Case-close.

ui.signal: Service Console layout: header highlights panel (role, category, FID, Case timeline), category-driven sub-tab switching (4 tabs). Cross-channel 30-day Case timeline filter. Omni-Channel widget + LMD disposition picklist. Requires Lightning App Builder + custom tab components.

sharing_security.signal: Case RecordType=Complaint layout. Permission set for QSR agents. Standard.

size_rationale: L — dual L drivers: (1) the Voice Call→Case Flow with branching match logic and 3+ DML paths, (2) the Service Console layout with category-driven sub-tab switching across 4 categories. Together these are the structural backbone of the agent workspace.
risks: Case dedup match key (FID + phone + 30-day window) needs validation (Open Q6) — a bad key inflates duplicate Cases. Sub-tab switching requires all 4 Lightning components (E04–E07) to be built before full Console layout can be tested end-to-end.

title: Order Lookup Lightning Component + OMS Integration

data_model.signal: Read-only display — no new Salesforce objects persisted.

automation.signal: Apex controller for callout + response parsing. No complex DML.

integration.signal: Two external API callouts: (1) OMS order lookup by order ID/customer name/FID+time-window, (2) Subway API adapter for POS-received status + adapter timestamp + driver-assigned status. Named Credentials, OAuth, error handling, timeout/retry, field mapping. API contracts not finalized — Unknown confidence. ASSUMED: REST/JSON, reasonable latency.

ui.signal: Custom LWC with Apex controller: order ID/customer name/FID+time-window query inputs, results table (POS status, Subway API timestamp, driver status), LMD652 disposition shortcut. Embedded in Service Console sub-tab.

size_rationale: L — dual L drivers: custom LWC + Apex (UI), and a dual-system integration (OMS + Subway API adapter) with unresolved API contracts. Confidence Unknown because both API contracts are open — this is the highest-risk build item and the band could widen to XL if APIs are complex or latency/auth patterns are non-standard.
risks: CRITICAL: OMS API contract (Michelle Fultz) and Subway API adapter contract not finalized. Auth, data model, error handling all TBD. If APIs require complex transform or are non-REST, size escalates to XL. Dependency on Michelle Fultz team responsiveness is the critical path.

title: Driver Lightning Component + LMD Un-batch API Integration

data_model.signal: Driver status displayed read-only. Un-batch action outcome written to Case notes. No new persistent objects.

automation.signal: Salesforce Flow or Apex callout for LMD un-batch API action. Omni-Channel warm-transfer action config.

integration.signal: Two external systems: (1) Spark driver systems for current driver ETA + assignment status (read), (2) LMD un-batch API (write/action). Un-batch is an action callout — not just read. API contracts not finalized (Open: Edwin Ortiz). Error handling, idempotency, and rollback on failed un-batch are design decisions.

ui.signal: Custom LWC: current driver display, ETA, wait-time-so-far counter, one-click Un-batch button (action-in-context), warm-transfer action to Spark queue. Embedded in Driver sub-tab.

size_rationale: L — custom LWC + action-oriented integration (un-batch is a write/action, not just a lookup). Unknown confidence because LMD un-batch API contract (Edwin Ortiz) is not finalized. The one-click Un-batch action has error/rollback complexity not present in the Order Lookup.
risks: LMD un-batch API contract (Edwin Ortiz) critical dependency. Un-batch is an action with side effects — failure handling and idempotency design needed. Spark driver ETA API: unknown latency/freshness characteristics. Could widen to XL if un-batch has complex orchestration.

title: Complaint Intake Lightning Form + Allergen P0 Fast-Track

data_model.signal: Complaint RecordType on Case + custom fields (complaint type picklist, severity, customer contact, action taken, allergen flag, Compliance ack field).

automation.signal: Allergen checkbox → Flow: P0 alert to Compliance + Partner Services queue within 15 min (time-based action), notification, Case-close validation rule blocking save until Compliance ack=TRUE. ~20–25 Flow nodes, time-based path, cross-object validation. Regulatory requirement.

ui.signal: Custom LWC complaint intake form: 7 fields + allergen checkbox + action taken. Auto-populates linked Case. Standard-complexity LWC.

sharing_security.signal: RecordType=Complaint layout gating. Compliance acknowledgement field: write-restricted to Compliance profile. Regulatory overlay on a P0 path.

size_rationale: L — driven by the allergen/food-safety P0 Flow (time-based action, 15-min SLA, cross-object validation, compliance ack gating). The form itself is M but the regulatory automation adds L. Compliance on-call queue creation is an operational dependency.
risks: Compliance on-call queue does not exist today — owner + staffing decision (Open Q7) required before Flow can be fully configured and tested. Complaint hand-back policy not written (Open Q9). Allergen path is P0/regulatory — any gap here is a go-live blocker.

title: Item Signal Lightning Form + Catalog/Adapter Routing

data_model.signal: Child Case creation (RecordType=Item Signal or similar). Item ID, issue type picklist, duration picklist fields.

automation.signal: On form save: Flow creates child Case, routes via Omni-Channel or assignment rule to adapter/catalog queue. ~12–15 Flow nodes. Straightforward routing.

ui.signal: Custom LWC: item ID/name input, issue type picklist, duration picklist, save action. Standard-complexity component.

size_rationale: M — standard-complexity LWC form + Flow child Case creation + queue routing. No external API callout (signal lands on a Salesforce child Case routed to an internal queue). P1 — could be deferred to Phase 2.
risks: Item Signal triage owner not decided (Open Q8). Queue configuration depends on this decision. If routing requires an external Subway API call to signal OOS in real-time (vs. internal Case handoff), size escalates to L.

analytics_insights.signal: Native Salesforce reports on Voice Call + Case (call volume by category, AHT, LMD rate, complaint mix, item signal volume by store). Plus data pipe to Power BI LMD Dashboard — either CRM Analytics connector or a scheduled export/API feed. Data pipe scope TBD.

automation.signal: Scheduled data export or CRM Analytics recipe if data pipe is the chosen approach.
